speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a child presenting with a limp and localized pain but no fever. Where exactly is the pain located, and when did you first notice the limp?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The pain is in the left knee, but in children, hip pathology often refers pain to the knee. Does he experience any pain in his hip or groin area? Also, does the pain worsen when he takes his legs apart while lying down (abduction), or does it hurt when you try to bend his knee fully?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for confirming; the pain is strictly in the left knee with no hip or groin discomfort. To narrow this down, can you tell me if the pain gets worse when he runs or jumps, and does he have any history of a recent minor fall or injury?

REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP.
REQUEST TEST: Hip_X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text:
RESULTS: 
CBC: Normal
ESR: Normal
CRP: Normal
Hip_X-Ray: Flattening and fragmentation of the left femoral head consistent with Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Legg-Calvé-Perthes Disease.

The normal inflammatory markers combined with the X-ray findings of femoral head flattening and fragmentation confirm the diagnosis. Please ensure the patient avoids high-impact activities to protect the hip joint during treatment.
